resources.allowTrivial: The opening cold frame compares every RGB channel of the 1280x720 display, so the count is fixed by the viewport and the positive arm is compared on the same samples.
With the reset gate removed the opening frame still blends whatever the history buffer holds, so the contaminated count is a one-time measurement the run cannot change.
The resize cold frame compares every RGB channel of the 1280x480 display, so both arms are contrasted on identical sample sets.
The same control at the resize reset frame, whose freshly allocated history buffer is equally unwritten; both are single measurements taken before the assertion runs.
The frame is a reset frame by the provider's own report, which is what identifies it for the comparison; the removed gate is a shader concern and does not change that report.
The same counter runs in this arm over the same 1280x720 display, so its GPU visited count must equal the positive row's. A smaller count here would mean the count itself depends on the removed gate.
The resize reset frame counts the same 1280x480 display as the positive row, on the same sample of the run.

With the reset gate removed the counted share is whatever the depth test alone decides, so it stays a finite fraction of the display; the positive row owns the whole-raster claim and this row deliberately makes none.
